Plan approved by user on 2026-09-25 in session ses_f27692478ffeJeaC9d0iggZ2dG: "The plan looks good, go ahead and prepare the beadwork issues for implementation". This is architectural/planning approval, not final UX approval, implementation completion or permission to commit/push.

Full approved specification follows; historical no-Beadwork statements describe plan drafting, before this issue creation. Beadwork now owns progress.

# ZAQ Serving V1 — Implementation Plan

Status: proposed implementation plan; no application changes made.
Date: 2026-09-25.

## 1. Outcome and settled scope

Add a `:serving` role that runs local Hugging Face models through Nx, advertises its hardware capabilities, checks model eligibility before loading, and supports management and interactive testing through BO.

User decisions:

- Stay on **Nx 0.13.x**. `jev_nx` intentionally excludes Nx 1.x; do not override its constraints or undertake an upgrade.
- Use `jev_nx` for Laya rather than porting Laya or introducing Python.
- V1 supports four tasks: typed decisions, embeddings, PII detection, and small-LLM text generation.
- Every globally enabled model targets **all serving nodes**. Per-model deployment placement is future work.
- Engine coordinates configuration, eligibility, deployment, and playground calls.
- Include a BO playground that reuses the existing chat presentation where appropriate.
- Do not integrate Serving into Agent providers, ingestion embeddings, or other production consumers in V1.

This document uses proposed module names and contracts. Existing owners must be rechecked immediately before implementation. Durable execution steps belong in Beadwork once implementation is authorized; this external plan is the user-requested design artifact, not a second project tracker.

### Proposed defaults requiring architectural approval

- Management and playground access require an authenticated, current `super_admin` BO user. Existing BO authentication alone is insufficient for this policy.
- Eligible nodes may load while other nodes reject the model. The aggregate deployment remains partially ready, with per-node reasons.
- One selected compute device/backend per serving node in V1; multiple models may share its explicitly budgeted capacity. Enumerate all detected devices, but do not implement tensor parallelism or cross-device memory pooling.
- Model replacement is unload-then-load on each node, avoiding an unbudgeted double residency peak. A failed replacement is visible; automatic rollback is not assumed.
- Playground text/results are session-local and bounded, not stored as production conversations. Configuration, operation metadata, and deployment status are durable.

## 2. Discovery and reuse evidence

### Existing ZAQ infrastructure

| Evidence | Consequence |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/zaq/node_roles.ex`: fixed list of six roles, `ROLES` parsing, `:all` support | Extend the canonical role list and preserve existing defaults/validation. |
| `lib/zaq/application.ex`: role-specific supervisors plus shared Repo/PubSub/Oban infrastructure | Add a lightweight `Zaq.Serving.Supervisor`; follow existing deployment architecture, including shared infrastructure requirements. |
| `lib/zaq/node_router.ex`: role supervisor/API maps, `dispatch/1`, `dispatch_all/1` | Reuse role discovery and fan-out. `dispatch_all` performs synchronous calls in sequence, so handlers must acknowledge quickly. |
| `lib/zaq/event_hop.ex`: destination role, type, timestamp; no node selector | Explicit ready-instance routing needs a narrow router extension; there is no existing node selector to assume. |
| `lib/zaq/engine/api.ex`: domain event handlers | Add explicit serving-management domain actions; no generic remote module invocation. |
| `lib/zaq/system.ex` and existing global settings | Reuse configuration conventions, but put model catalog/deployments in a cohesive Engine serving context rather than growing the large system context with runtime lifecycle logic. |
| `lib/zaq_web/live/bo/ai/bo_actor.ex`: trusted BO actor construction | Reuse actor construction; authorize the current user at the new Engine boundary. A nil identity or client-supplied bypass flag grants nothing. |
| `lib/zaq_web/live/bo/auth_hook.ex`: authentication/password-change handling | Add explicit feature authorization; do not treat this hook as an admin check. |
| `lib/zaq_web/chat/{composer,transcript}.ex`, `lib/zaq_web/components/chat_message.ex` | Reuse presentation with small, backward-compatible extension/extraction; composer currently requires retrieval-filter assigns. |
| Searches across `lib/zaq`, Actions/tools, and domain operation names found no local HF loading/unloading/hardware-eligibility implementation | New serving operations are needed. Recheck discovery during implementation rather than inventing a second existing operation. |

The default `:all` topology must remain usable: start lightweight serving control processes, but perform no model download or model allocation unless a model is enabled. Native backends are packaged for the deployment profile and initialized only by Serving. A missing/incompatible optional backend is a capability result, not a crash of an unrelated BO/Engine role.

### Dependency baseline

| Dependency | Planned constraint | Evidence/qualification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `nx` | `~> 0.13.0` | Explicit patch-series pin matches the user's decision; `~> 0.13` alone would allow later 0.x minors. |
| `exla` | `~> 0.13.0` | CPU host and Linux CUDA backend, with platform-appropriate XLA artifacts/drivers. |
| `bumblebee` | `~> 0.7.1` | Published dependencies admit Nx 0.13.x and Axon 0.8.x. |
| `jev_nx` | `~> 0.2.0` | Published package and upstream source expose Laya/Nx serving. |
| `emlx` | `~> 0.4.0`, macOS build profile | Package metadata admits Nx 0.x including 0.13; upstream `jev_nx` uses EMLX 0.4 in macOS development/tests. Actual four-task compatibility must be tested. |

Pin the resolved dependency graph in `mix.lock`; verify the project's Elixir/OTP/native-toolchain requirements. `jev_nx` 0.2 declares Elixir `~> 1.18`. Do not use Nx 1.x documentation as proof of Nx 0.13 APIs. Do not copy the `jev_nx` README's older Emily example: current source uses EMLX. No ONNX/Python path is needed for this plan.

### Initial checkpoint acceptance candidates

| Task | Candidate | What is verified now / what remains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typed decisions | `convaiinnovations/laya` | `Jev.Nx.Laya` exists, with encoder/head/tokenizer loading. Verify the pinned repository layout, selected checkpoint, output types, and backend behavior. |
| Embeddings | `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` | HF config is `BertModel`, present in Bumblebee 0.7.1. Verify pooling, normalization, sentence-transformer configuration, weights and tokenizer. |
| PII | `gravitee-io/bert-small-pii-detection` | HF config is `BertForTokenClassification`, present in Bumblebee 0.7.1, with concrete PII BIO labels. Verify weights, tokenization, original-text offsets, and output grouping. |
| Small LLM | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` | HF config is `Qwen3ForCausalLM`, present in Bumblebee 0.7.1. Verify weights, precision, tokenizer/chat template, streaming, and bounded generation. |

These are candidates, not claims of completed execution tests. Resolve immutable HF revisions during the first work package. Other HF repositories can be configured when their task/architecture/artifacts pass the supported adapter contract; these four examples are not a hardcoded catalog of all permitted repository IDs.

Do not assume similar families are interchangeable. Discovery found Qwen2 and DeBERTa-v2 checkpoints whose architecture names are not in the inspected Bumblebee 0.7.1 architecture mapping; reject unsupported architectures rather than attempting arbitrary remote code.

## 3. Boundaries and module responsibilities

### Control flow

1. BO builds a trusted actor and dispatches an explicit Engine event.
2. Engine authorizes, validates, persists desired configuration, and coordinates operations.
3. Engine uses NodeRouter events to reach Serving.
4. Serving owns its filesystem cache, backend, admission accounting, and `Nx.Serving` processes.
5. Serving reports bounded status/results to Engine; Engine publishes authorized BO updates.

Model weights/tensors never transit NodeRouter or the database. Each serving node downloads its own immutable artifacts. Model cache access is owned by Serving, not the Storage-role user-file API.

### Proposed source map

| Path/module area | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `lib/zaq/serving/supervisor.ex`, `api.ex` | Role startup, explicit role action handlers. |
| `lib/zaq/serving/capabilities.ex`, `hardware/*`, `backend.ex` | Hardware snapshots, platform probes, usable backend/device selection. |
| `lib/zaq/serving/hugging_face.ex`, `artifact_cache.ex` | HF metadata/revision resolution, controlled downloads, local artifact integrity/cache lifecycle. |
| `lib/zaq/serving/model_adapter.ex`, `adapters/{laya,bumblebee}.ex` | Common task contract, upstream model loading/serving, task-specific input/output adaptation. |
| `lib/zaq/serving/eligibility.ex` | Pure compatibility/resource evaluation from a model manifest, execution profile, and capability snapshot. |
| `lib/zaq/serving/runtime.ex`, `model_state.ex` | Serialized reservations and lifecycle, dynamic children, stale-result fencing, request admission and draining. |
| `lib/zaq/engine/serving.ex`, `engine/serving/*` | Catalog schemas, desired state, node observations, reconciliation, operation tracking, execution routing. |
| `lib/zaq/engine/serving/actions/*` | Focused reusable management/test Actions delegating to the owning context. |
| `lib/zaq_web/live/bo/system/local_models_live.ex` | Global settings management screen; queries/mutations via Engine. |
| `lib/zaq_web/live/bo/system/model_playground_live.ex` | Bounded interactive playground state and Engine request/update handling. |
| `lib/zaq_web/components/design_system/*` | Approved reusable model status/result components and Storybook stories. |

Keep modules proportional to their actual responsibility; do not create a class/module per tuple or a second plugin discovery framework. Only introduce behaviours at real platform/model/provider boundaries. Read and confirm every edited module's `@moduledoc` before adding responsibilities.

### Adapter contract

Use two runtime adapters initially: Laya via `jev_nx`, and Bumblebee with task-specific serving builders. A small explicit registry maps supported task/architecture combinations to adapters. No module names, atoms, or executable code are accepted from BO/HF metadata.

- `inspect_manifest`: derive architecture, artifact layout, supported tasks/types and execution bounds without allocating model tensors.
- `estimate`: return a versioned resource estimate with provenance, assumptions, supported backend/dtype combinations, and unresolved fields.
- `load/build_serving`: consume an approved local artifact directory and a resolved execution profile.
- `validate_input` and `normalize_output`: enforce each task's boundary contract.
- `run`: execute one bounded request or generation stream using the correct registered model serving.

The Laya adapter delegates to `Jev.Nx` instead of recreating model math, tokenization, or typed-answer decoding. Verify the package's per-serving invocation API; do not change global `:jev_nx, :serving` configuration for each selected model. Use registered serving references/processes and explicit backend/compiler options. Likewise, do not mutate a node-wide default backend when switching models.

## 4. Durable data and runtime DTOs

### Engine persistence

Use focused tables and Ecto schemas under `Zaq.Engine.Serving`, with migrations in `priv/repo/migrations/`:

1. **Model**: UUID, display name, task enum, source `hugging_face`, repository, requested revision, resolved commit, artifact subfolder/manifest fingerprint, optional existing credential reference, desired state `loaded|unloaded`, execution profile, configuration generation, timestamps. No target-node list in V1.
2. **ServingNode**: stable deployment-provided node key, observed BEAM identity, boot incarnation, last-seen time, capabilities DTO and schema version. An operator-supplied stable node key distinguishes replacement from an additional replica; never create atoms from stored node strings.
3. **Deployment**: unique model/node pair, requested/observed configuration generation, node incarnation, lifecycle state, operation ID, eligibility summary, bounded error code, last transition and last report times.
4. **Operation**: UUID, actor ID, kind, model/generation, idempotency key, requested/completed times and per-node outcomes. Persist lifecycle metadata, not inference text/tokens/weights. Inference request tracking may remain bounded ephemeral state with audit metadata where existing conventions require it.

Use optimistic locking/configuration generations for edits and database uniqueness for repeated submissions. Do not represent model configuration as unrelated string keys in `system_config`.

### Runtime capability DTO

Include observation time/expiry, OS/version, architecture, CPU/logical-core information, total and currently available host memory, effective process/container limits, devices and stable local identifiers, device memory type, total/free or unknown memory, installed/usable backends with probe failures, supported dtypes, selected backend/device, cache capacity, and model/resource reservations.

Distinguish physical RAM from cgroup limits and distinguish dedicated VRAM from Apple unified memory. Missing measurements are `unknown`, never zero or unlimited. Probe Linux cgroup v1/v2 where applicable. Device marketing names are informational, not proof of usability.

### Execution profile

Bound input length, batch size, queued/running requests, precision, and shape buckets. Additional task limits:

- Decisions: number of questions, options/criteria, and state/question token budget.
- Embeddings: number/length of texts, pooling and normalization.
- PII: maximum text length/window count, label mapping, span aggregation policy, confidence threshold.
- Generation: context and prompt lengths, maximum new tokens, KV-cache budget, concurrency, stop conditions and approved sampling settings.

The same validated profile feeds estimation, compilation, request admission, and BO controls. Changing it increments the model generation and requires re-eligibility. Reject or explicitly report truncation; never silently discard user text.

## 5. Backend selection and eligibility

### Platform matrix

- Linux x86_64 CPU: EXLA host.
- Linux x86_64 NVIDIA: EXLA CUDA after a successful backend probe, with CPU fallback only when the model/profile also qualifies on CPU.
- Native macOS arm64: EMLX Metal after a successful probe; validated CPU fallback where packaged.
- Other Unix/CPU architecture combinations: report discovered capabilities, but mark supported only after release-build and execution verification. “Unix” is not a single acceleration platform.

Separate installed backend, usable backend, and model-compatible backend. Select a node backend deterministically at boot from validated candidates and a node-local administrator override. Missing GPU drivers or a failed probe must not silently produce a false GPU-ready report. Do not assume Linux containers on a Mac have Metal access.

### Two-stage model checks

1. Inspect HF metadata, required files, architecture, task, dtype and weight headers/size information before fetching large artifacts. A manifest inspection itself may require bounded metadata/header requests.
2. After download, validate the immutable files and refresh capability/resource data before reserving load/compile memory. Readiness requires successful warm-up and a task-specific smoke input.

Return `eligible`, `ineligible`, or `unknown`, plus reason codes, estimated bytes by memory domain, execution limits, estimate version/confidence and snapshot expiry. An unknown resource requirement does not automatically authorize loading.

Estimate resident weights, host staging/conversion copies, compilation peak, activations, batch workspace, generation KV cache, backend allocator behavior, and configured system headroom. Account for existing models and pending operations; never sum Apple RAM and GPU memory as separate budgets. Validate disk download/extraction needs separately.

Runtime serializes local admissions and reservations across all models. Capability reads are advisory: admission rechecks atomically. Avoid double-counting committed model allocations already reflected in live free-memory telemetry while still subtracting pending, not-yet-materialized reservations. Specify/test this accounting with separate committed and pending ledgers.

Bound serving input shapes to prevent arbitrary recompilation and unplanned memory expansion. Backend memory may remain cached after unload; refresh measurement/allocator state before treating it as reusable. Estimates reduce OOM risk but cannot guarantee survival of competing OS allocations or native failures.

## 6. Lifecycle and all-node reconciliation

### State model

`unloaded → inspecting → blocked | downloading → loading → warming → ready → draining → unloaded`

Failures carry the failed stage and safe error code. `offline`/`stale` are node-observation conditions rather than fictional successful runtime transitions. Unload releases runtime resources; cached files are retained within a quota and eviction policy that never removes in-use/pending-load artifacts.

Engine persists desired state before notifying nodes. Serving startup announces its incarnation and requests the authoritative desired snapshot from Engine. Periodic reconciliation repairs missed announcements or updates. Multiple Engine instances may send the same generation; local idempotency and database constraints prevent duplicate side effects. No long transaction spans network/download/compilation work.

For each model/node/generation:

- Fan-out commands acknowledge acceptance/rejection quickly and return an operation ID.
- Serving runs supervised background jobs and emits bounded progress reports.
- Duplicate commands return the existing operation or terminal state.
- Late download/load/stream results are fenced by generation and boot incarnation.
- A newer unload cancels queued/loading intent and discards late success; free the resulting resource safely if native work finishes later.
- Changes to the model revision/profile drain the old serving before loading its replacement.
- Known offline nodes keep the aggregate from claiming ready everywhere. Distinguish “ready on all connected nodes” from “ready on all registered nodes.”
- A returned node rechecks eligibility and converges to the latest desired state, including unloads/deletions missed while offline.

Use a full versioned desired snapshot or explicit retained tombstones to prevent deleted models from being resurrected. Prefer unload then catalog deletion with reconciliation generation tracking; do not rely solely on a one-time delete broadcast.

Deleting a node record is an explicit administrative removal of a decommissioned replica, not automatic forgetting of an offline target. The runtime must release reservations on every task exit/failure path; node restart invalidates prior incarnation state and never restores a “ready” flag without loading.

## 7. Events, Actions and ready-instance routing

### Proposed public BO-to-Engine actions

| Action | Input | Result/side effects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `serving_list_models`, `serving_list_nodes`, `serving_get_operation` | Filters or known IDs | Secret-free catalog/status DTOs; no model loading. |
| `serving_save_model` | Validated model specification, expected generation | Persist catalog revision/profile; immutable HF resolution is part of inspection. |
| `serving_check_eligibility` | Model ID/generation | Operation ID and eventual per-node assessments; does not allocate weights. |
| `serving_set_desired_state` | Model ID, expected generation, loaded/unloaded, idempotency key | Durable desired state and asynchronous all-node convergence. |
| `serving_delete_model` | Model ID/generation | Unload/delete intent with reconciliation protection. |
| `serving_test_model` | Model ID/generation, task input/profile subset, request ID | Bounded request acceptance, then typed result or sequenced stream. |
| `serving_cancel_test` | Request ID | Ownership-authorized cancellation; best effort for native work, guaranteed suppression of stale UI output. |

Node-local role actions include capabilities, inspect, reconcile, status, execute and cancel. The Serving API accepts authorized Engine-coordinated commands with server-owned request/generation/node context. Do not expose an Agent tool or workflow registry entry merely because an operation uses a Jido Action.

### Routing a playground request

Deployment fan-out and inference routing are different concerns. A model can be blocked on one replica and ready on another.

Extend `NodeRouter.dispatch/1` with an optional **trusted internal target selector** in event options (or an equivalent narrow existing-router API after final source review). It must resolve only to a currently discovered node advertising the requested role, preserve existing local-first behavior when omitted, and return an explicit unavailable error rather than falling back to an arbitrary node. Never convert browser-provided node strings into atoms.

Engine selects a fresh ready instance of the requested model and generation, then passes this internal selector. This enables one request to execute once; it does not add a per-model deployment target setting. This small router extension requires regression tests and architectural approval.

Serving revalidates model generation/readiness and execution capacity before accepting. On a rejection known to occur before acceptance, Engine may select another ready replica. On an ambiguous RPC timeout after possible acceptance, query the original request ID or surface an uncertain/unavailable status; do not duplicate computation blindly.

BO receives a request ID immediately. For streaming, Serving emits sequenced chunks/completion to the Engine coordinator for that request, which relays to an authorized, session-scoped PubSub topic. Track the requesting process/coordinator incarnation; disconnect/restart cancels or expires the bounded execution. No direct BO-to-Serving call is introduced.

Typed errors include unauthorized, invalid_specification, unsupported_task/architecture/format/backend/precision, metadata_incomplete, insufficient_memory/disk, node_unavailable, stale_generation, model_not_ready, busy, download_failed, warmup_failed, timeout and cancelled. Do not return raw exceptions containing secrets or test input.

### Action reuse assessment

| Operation | Decision and evidence | Owning implementation / verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Role discovery and fan-out | Reuse `NodeRouter.dispatch_all/1`; exact behavior inspected | Router owns transport; assert all local/remote role instances receive short commands and per-node failures remain distinguishable. |
| Ready-instance dispatch | Extend existing NodeRouter; EventHop has no target field today | Trusted discovered-node selection, preserving default dispatch; test invalid/offline/wrong-role selection. |
| Model inspection and eligibility | New focused Action(s); no matching HF/local model operation found | Engine coordinator delegates node evaluation to Serving; typed contracts and no allocation in inspection. |
| Desired-state changes and deletion | New focused Actions; generic system config setters do not own replica lifecycle | Engine catalog/reconciler; permissions, idempotency, generations, partial failure and restart tests. |
| Playground execution/cancel | New focused Actions; existing Agent inference has different execution and product boundaries | Engine execution coordinator + Serving adapters; validate task schemas, authorization, lifecycle and stream ownership. |
| Tensor execution/model builders | Reuse `Jev.Nx`, `Bumblebee.Text` and `Nx.Serving` | Adapter tests demonstrate delegation and task-normalized results; no Laya reimplementation. |
| Hardware probing, cache file work, local reservations | Local-only implementation details with lifecycle ownership | Serving internals; creating independent agent/workflow Actions would expose unsafe partial operations. |
| Global read DTOs | Local context queries behind Engine domain API | Shared source of truth, authorization and secret-free projection tests. |
| BO actor, credentials, outbound HTTP | Reuse existing owners after callsite verification | No parallel secret store or identity policy. Test nil actor, revoked user and redaction. |

Programmatic Jido Actions execute via the validated `Jido.Exec` path rather than calling `run/2` directly. Flow remains API → Action → owning context → role event/runtime; no context → Action → same-context cycle.

## 8. HF artifacts, credentials and data handling

- Resolve a repository/revision to a commit and enumerate only the adapter-required files. Follow the model's real subfolder layout, including Laya encoder/head/tokenizer files.
- Enforce bounded metadata/download sizes, cache paths beneath the configured root, integrity checks where upstream provides hashes, atomic temporary-file promotion and incomplete-download cleanup.
- Use the established outbound HTTP policy/transport. Account for legitimate HF CDN redirects without forwarding authorization to unrelated hosts or bypassing policy.
- Prefer supported safetensors artifacts. Never execute repository Python or `trust_remote_code`; reject formats/layouts the adapter cannot safely support.
- For private/gated HF models, store only an existing Connect credential reference in the model row. Reuse encrypted API-key storage and trusted runtime credential resolution; no plaintext token field in model settings. Report inaccessible/gated artifacts as eligibility failures with redacted reasons.
- Mark playground request/result events confidential using the existing NodeRouter envelope mechanism and propagate it to child events. PII examples can contain actual sensitive text; keep logs, observer events and operation rows free of that payload.
- Bound UI history, vector previews, stream size and operation retention. Audit IDs/status/timing, not user text or raw tensors.

## 9. BO pages and task contracts

Add an authenticated Global Settings entry pointing to a dedicated Local Models LiveView, rather than embedding runtime orchestration in the large existing `SystemConfigLive`.

### Management page

- Model list: task, repository/revision, desired state, aggregate readiness and per-node status.
- Add/edit: HF repository/revision, optional credential reference, task, validated task profile. Show resolved immutable revision.
- Nodes panel: online/stale/offline, backend/device, effective memory/capacity, capability freshness and reasons a backend is unavailable.
- Eligibility drawer: compatibility checks, estimated resource breakdown, allowed limits and node-specific rejection reasons.
- Operations: inspect/check, load, unload, retry, remove; display progress and reconcile after reconnect.
- No deployment node picker in V1.

### Model playground

Use `bo_layout`, the existing composer/transcript/user/assistant message presentation, and approved DesignSystem components. Inspect component attributes and event contracts before reuse. Extend/extract only the cohesive presentation needed to hide retrieval-specific controls and render custom result content; preserve existing chat behavior and tests.

| Task | Input | Result rendering and correctness contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Decisions | Shared state and named typed questions; bounded choices/criteria | Typed answers, probabilities/confidence where supplied; never coerce `noul` probability into a fabricated certainty. |
| Embeddings | One or more text inputs; optional pair comparison | Vector dimension, norm, bounded numeric preview and cosine similarity between embeddings of the same model/profile; no fabricated prose reply. |
| PII | Text and approved threshold | Original-text span highlights, entity labels/confidences, redacted preview; offsets refer to original UTF-8 text with one documented offset convention and tested UI conversion. |
| Generation | Prompt or bounded multi-turn messages, supported generation parameters | Streaming text, stop/cancel, token counts if exposed, duration and explicit truncation/context errors. Apply a validated model-specific chat template; use prompt mode when no supported template exists. |

Every result shows model ID/revision/generation, executing node, backend/device, timing and effective parameters. PII highlighting uses escaped text, correct overlapping-span resolution and right-to-left replacement or equivalent offset-safe redaction. Text beyond supported PII context is explicitly rejected or processed through a verified bounded window policy; never imply unchecked text was scanned.

Input profiles remain server enforced. Cancelling, navigating away, unloading a model, or receiving a stale generation prevents subsequent chunks from being appended to the wrong result card.

## 10. Implementation work packages and test-first delivery

Create one Beadwork issue per work package below, splitting adapter implementations further when independently reviewable. Add an architectural approval issue before implementation and a separate human UX/UI approval issue before feature E2E authoring. IDs below are planning labels, not created tickets.

### S1 — Pin dependencies and validate four task adapters

- **Files/specification:** `mix.exs`, `mix.lock`, platform build configuration; `serving/model_adapter.ex`, `serving/adapters/{laya,bumblebee}.ex`. Implement the common contract and select immutable acceptance checkpoints. Validate EMLX 0.4/EXLA 0.13 APIs against installed versions. Avoid broad framework construction.
- **Tests first:** task input/output contract fixtures, unsupported-task/type/profile cases; integration harness for local checkpoints and tiny deterministic models; reference Laya golden cases from upstream where suitable.
- **Paths validated:** correct model/serving selection with two models loaded; CPU and accelerator results within documented tolerances; Laya choice/score/noul; embedding pooling/normalization; PII labels/offsets; generation template/stop behavior. Hardware tests must report unavailable runners, not a false pass.
- **Mocks:** external HF HTTP only; real Nx computation for adapter behavior. Use small local fixtures for ordinary CI and explicitly scheduled actual-model runs for acceptance.
- **Docs:** dependency/platform matrix and task support section in new `docs/services/serving.md`; update `docs/dev-setup.md` build requirements. Module docs explain ownership.
- **Reuse:** upstream model/task/serving builders; local adapters normalize contracts. Block completion if any of the four task families lacks a working checkpoint; replacing a candidate needs documented evidence, not silent scope removal.

### S2 — Serving role and real capability discovery

- **Files/specification:** role/application/router maps; `serving/{supervisor,api,capabilities,backend}.ex`, `serving/hardware/*`; existing deployment files discovered before editing. Lightweight boot, profile-specific native dependencies, explicit capability DTO and backend selection.
- **Tests first:** role parsing/default `:all`/startup; capability parser fixtures; missing libraries/drivers; stale/unknown values; OS versus container limits; unified-memory accounting; selection override and CPU fallback.
- **Paths validated:** BO/Engine-only startup, serving-only startup, mixed roles; no enabled models means no download/allocation; failed accelerator probes produce actionable capabilities.
- **Mocks:** no internal blanket mocks; pure fixture parsing and controlled production probe boundaries, plus real hardware smoke tests.
- **Docs:** `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/services/serving.md`, `docs/dev-setup.md`.
- **Reuse:** extend canonical role/router infrastructure; probes remain local-only.

### S3 — HF artifacts and model eligibility

- **Files/specification:** `serving/{hugging_face,artifact_cache,eligibility}.ex`; refine adapter metadata/estimates. Resolve immutable revisions, optional credentials, supported formats, bounded atomic cache and resource reports.
- **Tests first:** HTTP metadata/artifact fixtures; missing shards/files; interrupted download; access denied; redirect policy; credential redaction; path traversal; manifest mismatch; insufficient disk/RAM/VRAM; unknown requirements; stale capability expiry.
- **Property tests/paths:** increasing profile resource requirements cannot improve eligibility under identical capacity; no double counting unified memory; safe cache paths; unsupported architecture rejected before tensor allocation; exact Laya subdirectories preserved.
- **Mocks:** HF network edge only. Use isolated temporary directories, real file operations and pure eligibility calculations.
- **Docs:** serving eligibility/cache contract and system-config credential-reference behavior; API/module docs for all error states.
- **Reuse:** existing outbound HTTP/Connect security owners, upstream model metadata; new inspection/check Action contract consumes this domain implementation through Engine.

### S4 — Local multi-model runtime and admission

- **Files/specification:** `serving/{runtime,model_state}.ex`, serving registry/dynamic/task supervisors, API handlers. Serialize reservations, build named servings in background, warm before ready, bound queues, support draining/cancellation/cache retention.
- **Tests first:** concurrent loads whose sum exceeds capacity; load/compile/inference failure cleanup; duplicate load; unload during download/compile/run; newer generation wins; resource release; retained allocator memory; task/process crashes; deadline expiry.
- **Property tests/paths:** no admission exceeds the configured domain budget under arbitrary valid command sequences; stale completion cannot revive unloaded/newer-generation models; model A's unload/cancel cannot affect B.
- **Mocks:** only external HF calls. Exercise supervised processes with real tiny Nx models, explicit clocks/messages and per-test registries; no application-env mutation as a routine seam.
- **Docs:** serving lifecycle/reservation/cancellation guarantees and native-failure limitations.
- **Reuse:** `Nx.Serving`, Registry, OTP supervision; local-only lifecycle machinery.

### S5 — Engine catalog, authorization, Actions and all-node convergence

- **Files/specification:** `engine/serving.ex`, catalog/deployment/node/operation schemas and migrations, coordinator/reconciler, `engine/serving/actions/*`, Engine API/supervisor. Implement section 4/7 contracts, current-user authorization, durable desired state and full-snapshot/tombstone reconciliation.
- **Tests first:** unauthorized/nil/inactive/non-admin actors; invalid specs; optimistic conflicts; idempotent saves/commands; multiple Engine senders; one failed/offline node; newly joined/restarted node; deletion missed while offline; stale incarnation reports.
- **Paths validated:** zero serving nodes retains desired state and reports unavailable; eligible nodes load despite blocked peers; ready-everywhere never hides known offline targets; role operations accept short commands and expose progress separately.
- **Mocks:** HTTP edge only; use real context/schema logic and controlled in-process/distributed role fixtures, not mocks of the canonical operation implementation.
- **Docs:** Engine ownership, serving event contracts, system configuration, architecture, migration/operator guidance.
- **Reuse:** `dispatch_all`, existing actor/credential/config seams; new validated Actions delegate to the context. No registry exposure to Agent tools/workflows.

### S6 — Ready-instance dispatch and typed playground execution

- **Files/specification:** narrow `node_router.ex` extension and behavior contract as required; Engine serving execution coordinator; Serving execute/cancel handlers; task input/output DTOs. Select a fresh ready replica internally and return request ID, bounded result/stream and provenance.
- **Tests first:** omitted selector preserves routing; selected target must advertise role; bad/offline target never falls through; correct model/generation; pre-accept busy retries versus ambiguous post-accept timeout; duplicate request IDs; stale/disordered stream chunks; disconnect/cancel; request-owner checks.
- **Paths validated:** one request executes on one ready node despite a blocked peer; model unload/drain races; context/question/output limits; confidential envelopes omit text/results from observers. Verify actual multi-node delivery in a bounded distributed integration test.
- **Mocks:** external HF only; real router/role handlers and deterministic tiny model execution. Resolve runtime dependencies through production `Zaq.Config`/event/startup seams.
- **Docs:** NodeRouter selector contract in architecture; serving task/event/stream contract; module API docs.
- **Reuse:** extend NodeRouter rather than bypassing it with ad-hoc RPC; new test/cancel Actions share Engine execution logic.

### S7 — BO management and reusable model playground

- **Files/specification:** new system LiveViews, `lib/zaq_web/router.ex`, actual sidebar/global-settings navigation owner, targeted chat/DesignSystem components and Storybook. Wire sections 8/9 through Engine events. Apply relevant design/extract/replace approval procedures before component changes.
- **Tests first:** LiveView/component tests for authorization, validation, immutable revision display, per-node eligibility/progress, partial readiness, operation reconnect, each task's input/result card, retry/unload, stream cancellation and escaped PII/text rendering.
- **Paths validated:** no nodes, all ready, partially ready, stale/offline, unknown resources, rejected input, loader error, wrong-generation result, long/Unicode PII text, bounded embeddings/history. Existing chat presentation behavior remains covered.
- **Mocks:** HF edge only; use Engine public boundaries and deterministic local runtime fixtures rather than LiveView-owned business logic.
- **Docs:** new local-model management/playground user guide; Storybook stories; BO guide links if a reusable component is added; existing design contract remains authoritative.
- **Reuse:** `bo_layout`, composer/transcript/message components; extend/extract only approved cohesive slices.

### S8 — Platform acceptance, UX approval, E2E, documentation and final gates

- **Files/specification:** focused integration/property/platform tests, approved feature E2E, CI/deployment profile files, serving/operator documentation and docs index links.
- **Tests first:** define acceptance scenarios before coding earlier steps; author new feature E2E only after completed-feature human UX/UI approval. Cover add → inspect → load → test each task → unload, partial eligibility, restart convergence and authorization failure.
- **Paths validated:** all four tasks on CPU, Linux NVIDIA and native Apple Silicon for configurations claiming support. Record exact hardware, OS, driver/backend versions, checkpoint commits, dtype/profile, peak observed memory and output tolerances. Unsupported combinations remain explicitly ineligible; required missing hardware validation is a completion blocker.
- **Mocks:** no simulated accelerator results presented as platform acceptance; HF edge fixtures remain suitable for ordinary deterministic E2E/CI where model artifacts are preloaded.
- **Docs:** `docs/services/serving.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/services/engine.md`, `docs/services/system-config.md`, `docs/dev-setup.md`, new operator/user guides and `docs/README.md`; add only links at routing/index owners.
- **Reuse/validation:** follow `docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md#phase-4--validate` and later review/coverage/final-approval phases. Run `mix q` plus issue-isolated tests during delivery; final `mix precommit` after all required implementation, E2E/review/coverage work. Do not repeat or weaken passing assertions merely to reach a numeric target.

### Dependency graph

Architectural approval precedes implementation. S1 and S2 are independent roots after approval; S3 follows their model/capability contracts; S4 follows S3; S5 follows S4; S6 follows S5; S7 follows S6; S8 final acceptance follows S7 and the human UX/UI approval gate.

S1 + S2 → S3 → S4 → S5 → S6 → S7 → human UX/UI approval → feature E2E/final S8.

The S1/S2 convergence is intentional: eligibility needs both supported model metadata and measured hardware capabilities. Split large issues by owner/test surface, preserving these prerequisites. CI/unit/property testing and documentation happen within each step, not only at S8.

## 11. Completion criteria and unresolved evidence

V1 is complete when:

- A serving-only node advertises accurate supported capabilities without blocking boot on model work.
- All four task families have immutable, exercised reference checkpoints on the supported platform matrix.
- Every enabled model converges on all serving nodes, subject to explicit per-node eligibility; failed/offline nodes are visible.
- No unsupported/unknown configuration is silently accepted, and concurrent model admissions respect the declared budget.
- Restart, missed events, duplicate operations, unload/load races and stale results converge correctly.
- BO can manage models and test each task with correct typed rendering and provenance, using shared chat presentation.
- Engine remains the control/execution coordination boundary, without production Agent/ingestion provider wiring.
- Authorization, credential handling, privacy, unit/integration/property/platform and approved E2E checks pass under repository validation policy.

Evidence still required during implementation, rather than asserted by this plan:

1. The complete dependency graph resolves/builds on this repository's Elixir/OTP and every claimed release platform.
2. Each acceptance checkpoint's weights/tokenizer/layout works at a pinned commit; config architecture matching alone is insufficient.
3. EMLX 0.4 and EXLA 0.13 execute each adapter's required operators and precision, with measured peak memory and acceptable output differences.
4. Backend allocator telemetry/reclamation is reliable enough for documented admission accounting; unknown measurements remain conservative.
5. Current Connect credential-resolution and outbound HTTP callsites support node-local HF download with the intended administrative identity. Extend the canonical owners if necessary; do not create a private token fallback.
6. The proposed super-admin authorization, partial-deployment behavior and internal selected-node routing are approved architectural/product choices.

No implementation, dependency installation, model download, migration, test execution, Beadwork mutation, or Git mutation was performed while preparing this plan.

## 12. Sources inspected

- Repository policy owners: `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agent-tools.md`, `docs/agent-setup.md`, `docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md`, `docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md`, `docs/action-reuse.md`, `docs/documentation.md`, `docs/conventions.md`, `docs/code-quality.md`, `docs/testing-approach.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/services/{engine,system-config,bo-auth}.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `docs/bo-components.md`.
- [jev_nx source](https://github.com/dannote/jev_nx), [dependency declarations](https://github.com/dannote/jev_nx/blob/master/mix.exs), [published 0.2.0 metadata](https://hex.pm/api/packages/jev_nx/releases/0.2.0).
- [Bumblebee 0.7.1 task API](https://hexdocs.pm/bumblebee/0.7.1/Bumblebee.Text.html), [architecture mapping](https://github.com/elixir-nx/bumblebee/blob/v0.7.1/lib/bumblebee.ex), [package dependencies](https://hex.pm/api/packages/bumblebee/releases/0.7.1).
- [EXLA 0.13.0 metadata](https://hex.pm/api/packages/exla/releases/0.13.0), [EMLX 0.4.0 metadata](https://hex.pm/api/packages/emlx/releases/0.4.0).
- HF model cards/configs: [Laya](https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya), [MiniLM](https://huggingface.co/sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2), [BERT-small PII](https://huggingface.co/gravitee-io/bert-small-pii-detection), [Qwen3 0.6B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B).
